previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with acute abdominal pain and vomiting, consistent with a flare of her chronic pancreatitis, in the setting of recent methotrexate administration and dehydration. She was treated with IV fluids, anti-nausea medication, and pain control, with significant improvement. Imaging, including CT and ultrasound, showed no acute abdominal pathology or biliary disease. Labs revealed no elevation in lipase, supporting absence of acute pancreatitis. She tolerated advancement to a soft diet, remained symptom-free, and was discharged home on her baseline medications with instructions to follow up with her primary care provider. The hospital course was uncomplicated.
